gancho: O velcro não foi invenção da NASA. A ideia veio em 1941 a um engenheiro suíço que viu carrapichos grudados no pelo do seu cão, e ele levou dez anos para mecanizar a fabricação. A NASA só deu fama a ele.
explicacao: George de Mestral voltava de uma caçada nos Alpes com o cachorro quando resolveu olhar ao microscópio os carrapichos de bardana presos na roupa e no pelo do animal. Viu centenas de ganchinhos que se agarravam a qualquer coisa com laços, como tecido, pelo ou cabelo. A grande sacada foi encolher o velho fecho de gancho e ilhó: com ganchos minúsculos, cada um perde força, então é preciso uma superfície inteira deles, e nenhum precisa encontrar um par específico. O nome junta duas palavras francesas, velours (veludo) e crochet (gancho). Em Lyon, então um polo de tecelagem, os grandes do setor recusaram a ideia; só um tecelão ajudou, com tiras de algodão que logo se desfiavam. De Mestral passou ao náilon e, quase desistindo, resolveu os ganchos com uma tesoura: cortava a ponta dos laços tecidos. A patente suíça, pedida em 1951, saiu em 1955. Mesmo assim, o fecho parecia feito de retalhos baratos e demorou a pegar. A primeira grande vitrine foi a indústria aeroespacial, em trajes de astronautas difíceis de vestir e tirar. Como o uso só se espalhou depois disso, a NASA costuma levar, sem razão, o crédito pela invenção.

fontes.trecho: The original hook-and-loop fastener was conceived in 1941 by Swiss engineer George de Mestral, which he named velcro. The word Velcro is a portmanteau of two French words: "velours" meaning velvet, and "crochet" meaning hook. The idea came to him one day after he returned from a hunting trip with his dog in the Alps. He took a close look at the burs of burdock that kept sticking to his clothes and his dog's fur. He examined them under a microscope, and noted their hundreds of hooks that caught on anything with a loop, such as clothing, animal fur, or hair. [...] The big breakthrough de Mestral made was to think about hook-and-eye closures on a greatly reduced scale. [...] reducing the size of the hooks also reduced the strength, requiring more hooks for the same strength. The other difference is that hook-and-loop has indeterminate match-up between the hooks and eyes. [...] De Mestral's proposal was initially rejected by industry leaders when he took his idea to Lyon, which was then a center of weaving. He did manage to gain the assistance of one weaver, who produced two cotton strips based on de Mestral's designs. But because the cotton frayed and wore out relatively quickly, de Mestral began to investigate the use of synthetic fibers [...] De Mestral eventually selected nylon [...] On the verge of giving up, he had a new idea: he bought a pair of shears and trimmed the tops off the loops, thus creating hooks that would match up with the loops in the pile. [...] In all, it took ten years to create a mechanized process that worked. De Mestral submitted his idea for a patent in Switzerland in 1951, which was granted in 1955. [...] At the time, the fasteners looked as though they had been made from leftover bits of cheap fabric [...] the fabric got its first break when it was used in the aerospace industry to help astronauts maneuver in and out of bulky space suits. [...] As hook-and-loop fasteners became widely used only after NASA's adoption of the technology, NASA is popularly – and incorrectly – credited with its invention.

gancho: Trens-bala japoneses saindo de túneis davam um estrondo parecido com o de um avião supersônico. Para o Shinkansen 500, a solução foi um nariz longo e afilado, copiado do bico do martim-pescador.
explicacao: Dentro de um túnel, o ar empurrado pelo trem não tem para onde fugir. Formam-se ondas de compressão à frente dele, que se juntam numa onda de choque e estouram ao chegar à saída. É o "estrondo de túnel", que as pessoas percebem como o de um avião supersônico, embora o trem esteja bem abaixo da velocidade do som. A força da onda cresce com o cubo da velocidade, e no Japão, montanhoso e cheio de túneis, o fenômeno virou um dos principais limites para trens mais rápidos; uma lei fixa em 70 decibéis o ruído máximo em áreas residenciais. Os engenheiros da JR-West foram buscar a resposta numa ave que mergulha para pescar quase sem espirrar água: o martim-pescador. O bico dele é longo e pontudo e vai engrossando aos poucos da ponta até a cabeça. A frente do Shinkansen 500 imitou esse perfil. O trem entrou em serviço em 1997 e foi o primeiro Shinkansen a rodar a 300 km/h no serviço regular de passageiros. Segundo os relatos mais divulgados do caso, o redesenho reduziu o ruído e permitiu andar 10% mais rápido gastando 15% menos energia.

fontes.trecho: Tunnel boom is a loud boom sometimes generated by high-speed trains when they exit tunnels. [...] People perceive this sound similarly to that of a sonic boom from supersonic aircraft. However, unlike a sonic boom, tunnel boom is not caused by trains exceeding the speed of sound. [...] As a train passes through a tunnel, it creates compression waves in front of it. These waves coalesce into a shock wave that generates a loud boom when it reaches the tunnel exit. The strength of this wave is proportional to the cube of the train's speed [...] Tunnel boom has become a principal limitation to increased train speeds in Japan where the mountainous terrain requires frequent tunnels. Japan has enacted a law limiting noise to 70 dB in residential areas

The 500 series (500系, Go-hyaku-kei) is a Shinkansen high-speed train type operated by West Japan Railway Company (JR-West) [...] entering passenger service in March 1997. [...] It was the first Shinkansen train in Japan to operate at a maximum speed of 300 km/h (186 mph) in regular passenger service. [...] It used biomimicry to reduce energy consumption by 15%, increase speeds by 10% and reduce noise levels while increasing passenger comfort. This was done by designing the train's front to mimic the shape of a kingfisher's beak.

fontes.titulo: High Speed Train Inspired by the Kingfisher (AskNature, Biomimicry Institute)
fontes.trecho: When it would travel through tunnels, the wave would cause a loud "tunnel boom" at the exit, disturbing nearby residents. [...] They noticed how kingfisher birds are able to slice through the air and dive into the water to catch prey while barely making a splash. They then re-designed the front end of the train to mimic the shape of the kingfisher's beak. [...] It has a long, narrow pointed beak that allows it to enter the water while barely making a splash. The beak steadily increases in diameter from the tip to the head

gancho: A folha de lótus se limpa sozinha justamente por ser áspera. Saliências microscópicas cobertas de cera fazem só 0,6% da superfície da gota tocar a folha, e ela rola levando a sujeira junto.
explicacao: A intuição diria que o liso fica mais limpo, mas o lótus faz o contrário. A pele da folha tem papilas de 10 a 20 micrômetros de altura, recobertas por ceras que repelem água. Essa estrutura em dois níveis reduz tanto o contato que a gota fica quase esférica: em plantas assim, o ângulo de contato chega a 170 graus. As partículas de sujeira também mal tocam a folha e acabam presas com mais força à gota do que à superfície, por isso a água que rola as carrega. O mecanismo só foi explicado nos anos 1970, com o microscópio eletrônico de varredura. O botânico alemão Wilhelm Barthlott, pioneiro no uso sistemático desse microscópio em superfícies de seres vivos, começou a descrevê-lo com Ehler em 1977 e depois o batizou de "efeito lótus". Como o segredo está na forma, e não numa química exclusiva da planta, dá para copiá-lo: desde 1998 a marca Lotus Effect aparece em produtos, e há tintas, telhas e tecidos que se limpam com a chuva. O truque tem limite: depende da alta tensão superficial da água e não funciona com solventes orgânicos, por isso não protege contra pichação. Para a planta, ficar limpa ajuda a evitar fungos e algas e a não perder luz para a fotossíntese.

fontes.trecho: The self-cleaning property of ultrahydrophobic micro-nanostructured surfaces was studied by Wilhelm Barthlott and Ehler in 1977, who described such self-cleaning and ultrahydrophobic properties for the first time as the "lotus effect" [...] The epidermis of the lotus plant possesses papillae 10 μm to 20 μm in height and 10 μm to 15 μm in width on which the so-called epicuticular waxes are imposed. These superimposed waxes are hydrophobic and form the second layer of the double structure. [...] Plants with a double structured surface like the lotus can reach a contact angle of 170°, whereby the droplet's contact area is only 0.6%. [...] Dirt particles with an extremely reduced contact area are picked up by water droplets and are thus easily cleaned off the surface. If a water droplet rolls across such a contaminated surface the adhesion between the dirt particle, irrespective of its chemistry, and the droplet is higher than between the particle and the surface. [...] As this self-cleaning effect is based on the high surface tension of water it does not work with organic solvents. Therefore, the hydrophobicity of a surface is no protection against graffiti. This effect is of great importance for plants as a protection against pathogens like fungi or algae growth [...] Another positive effect of self-cleaning is the prevention of contamination of the area of a plant surface exposed to light resulting in reduced photosynthesis. [...] come from physical-chemical properties at the microscopic to nanoscopic scale rather than from the specific chemical properties of the leaf surface [...] Some nanotechnologists have developed treatments, coatings, paints, roof tiles, fabrics and other surfaces that can stay dry and clean themselves [...] its mechanism was explained only in the 1970s after the introduction of the scanning electron microscope.

Barthlott was the first botanist using high resolution scanning electron microscopy systematically in the research of biological surfaces since 1970. Most prominent among his results was the discovery of the self-cleaning effect of superhydrophobic micro- and nanostructured surfaces, which were technically realized with the trademark "Lotus Effect" from 1998 on, and resulting products distributed worldwide.

gancho: O Eastgate, em Harare, no Zimbábue, foi projetado para se refrescar sem ar-condicionado, imitando cupinzeiros. Depois, a explicação de como o próprio cupinzeiro se ventila mudou bastante.
explicacao: O centro comercial e de escritórios foi projetado pelo arquiteto zimbabuano Mick Pearce e construído pela firma britânica Ove Arup. Pearce se inspirou na arquitetura dos cupinzeiros, vistos como estruturas que mantêm a temperatura constante num clima de grandes variações. O prédio aproveita o ar frio da noite e o distribui durante o dia, por quarenta e oito dutos de tijolo, enquanto o ar quente sai pelo alto. Segundo os números divulgados, ele usa só 10% da energia de um prédio de porte parecido com refrigeração convencional. Já a biologia que serviu de modelo foi sendo revista. Uma proposta antiga era a de um termossifão: o calor do metabolismo da colônia faria o ar subir pelo monte e trocar calor e gases pelas paredes porosas. O fisiologista J. Scott Turner, estudando o cupim africano Macrotermes michaelseni, passou a ver o monte como um pulmão externo, cujo papel principal é a troca de gases respiratórios. Mais tarde, medições diretas do ar dentro de montes de outra espécie, Odontotermes obesus, mostraram ventilação movida pela oscilação diária de temperatura: de dia, os dutos externos e finos esquentam mais rápido que a chaminé central e o ar gira num sentido; à noite, no outro. Esse vaivém expulsa o gás carbônico do ninho.

fontes.trecho: The Eastgate Centre is a shopping centre and office block in the business centre of Harare, Zimbabwe, designed by Mick Pearce and built by Ove Arup and Partners. It is a unique example of building ventilated and cooled entirely by natural means. [...] It was designed by Zimbabwean architect Mick Pearce and built by engineers from British firm Ove Arup and Partners. [...] In-between the commercial spaces there are forty-eight brick funnels connected to each office and store. Funnels channel cool air from the basement and allow hot air to escape from the top of the building. [...] Eastgate incorporates passive cooling system, which conditions the interior air temperature by harvesting cool night air and dispensing it around the interior of Eastgate during the day. In his design Pearce was inspired by the termite mound's specific architecture that maintains a constant temperature in a "climate that fluctuates greatly [...] Passively cooled, Eastgate uses only 10% of the energy required by conventionally cooled building with similar space.

An early proposition suggested a thermosiphon mechanism. The heat created due to the metabolism of termites imparts sufficient buoyancy to the nest air to push it up into the mound and eventually to the mound's porous surface where heat and gases exchange with the atmosphere through the porous walls. [...] Research conducted on Macrotermes michaelseni mounds has shown that the primary role played by the mound is that of exchanging respiratory gases.
His extended organism idea was inspired by his work on termite mounds that clarified how the mound functions as an external lung for respiratory gas exchange for the colony as a whole.

fontes.titulo: King, Ocko e Mahadevan (2015). Termite mounds harness diurnal temperature oscillations for ventilation. PNAS
fontes.trecho: Although different hypotheses such as steady and fluctuating external wind and internal metabolic heating have been proposed for ventilating the mound, the absence of direct in situ measurement of internal air flows has precluded a definitive mechanism for this critical physiological function. By measuring diurnal variations in flow through the surface conduits of the mounds of the species Odontotermes obesus, we show that a simple combination of geometry, heterogeneous thermal mass, and porosity allows the mounds to use diurnal ambient temperature oscillations for ventilation. In particular, the thin outer flutelike conduits heat up rapidly during the day relative to the deeper chimneys, pushing air up the flutes and down the chimney in a closed convection cell, with the converse situation at night. These cyclic flows in the mound flush out CO2 from the nest and ventilate the colony

gancho: A Mercedes fez um carro-conceito imitando o peixe-cofre, tido como aerodinâmico e estável. Depois, um estudo mostrou que o formato do peixe nem reduz tanto o arrasto e, em vez de estabilizar, desestabiliza.
explicacao: O Mercedes-Benz Bionic, apresentado em 2005, foi modelado no peixe-cofre-amarelo, Ostracion cubicus, que vive em recifes de coral e tem as escamas, em placas hexagonais, fundidas numa carapaça em forma de caixa. A montadora escolheu o bicho pelo suposto baixo arrasto do corpo e pela rigidez da carapaça, e acreditava-se que o formato também ajudaria na estabilidade. A Mercedes anunciou para o carro um coeficiente de arrasto de 0,19. Em 2015, porém, biólogos mediram em tanque com água corrente, e simularam em computador, as forças sobre a carapaça de duas espécies de peixe-cofre. O desempenho em reduzir arrasto foi relativamente baixo comparado ao de peixes de formato mais comum. E a teoria de que a água correndo em volta da carapaça mantinha o peixe no rumo foi rejeitada: as forças medidas sempre tendiam a tirá-lo do curso. Isso resolveu um paradoxo. Um peixe que se estabilizasse sozinho combinaria mal com as manobras frequentes que os peixes-cofre fazem entre os corais. A instabilidade, ao contrário, ajuda a virar e inclinar com eficiência.

fontes.trecho: It was first introduced in 2005 at the DaimlerChrysler Innovation Symposium in Washington, D.C. The Bionic is modeled after the yellow boxfish, Ostracion cubicus [...] a marine fish that lives in coral reefs. Mercedes-Benz decided to model the Bionic after this fish due to the supposed low coefficient of drag of its body shape and the rigidity of its exoskeleton [...] It was believed that the shape of the boxfish would improve aerodynamics and stability. [...] However, in 2015, a paper in Journal of the Royal Society Interface stated that "The drag-reduction performance of the two boxfish species studied was relatively low compared with more generalized body shapes of fish". [...] Mercedes-Benz reported a drag coefficient of 0.19
Their hexagonal plate-like scales are fused into a solid, triangular or box-like carapace

fontes.titulo: Van Wassenbergh et al. (2015). Boxfish swimming paradox resolved. J R Soc Interface
fontes.trecho: The shape of the carapace protecting the body of boxfishes has been attributed an important hydrodynamic role in drag reduction and in providing automatic, flow-direction realignment and is therefore used in bioinspired design of cars. However, tight swimming-course stabilization is paradoxical given the frequent, high-performance manoeuvring that boxfishes display in their spatially complex, coral reef territories. Here, by performing flow-tank measurements of hydrodynamic drag and yaw moments together with computational fluid dynamics simulations, we reverse several assumptions about the hydrodynamic role of the boxfish carapace. Firstly, despite serving as a model system in aerodynamic design, drag-reduction performance was relatively low compared with more generalized fish morphologies. Secondly, the current theory of course stabilization owing to flow over the boxfish carapace was rejected, as destabilizing moments were found consistently. This solves the boxfish swimming paradox: destabilizing moments enhance manoeuvrability, which is in accordance with the ecological demands for efficient turning and tilting.

gancho: Os geckos, lagartixas que andam no teto, grudam sem cola nem ventosa: milhões de pelos microscópicos nos dedos aderem por forças de van der Waals, atrações fracas entre moléculas. E o 'adesivo' se limpa ao andar.
explicacao: Como os geckos aderem a quase qualquer material (o Teflon é exceção) foi assunto de estudo por mais de um século. Os dedos têm cristas cobertas de cerdas microscópicas, e cada cerda se divide em centenas de pontas achatadas, as espátulas. A equipe de Kellar Autumn mostrou que a adesão vem de forças de van der Waals, e não de cola, sucção ou química especial: os dedos do geco-tokaí aderiam tão bem a superfícies que repelem água quanto às que a atraem, e uma única cerda isolada se comportou do mesmo jeito. O poder vem do tamanho e da forma das pontas. Soltar também é engenhoso: ao aumentar para 30 graus o ângulo entre a cerda e a superfície, o gecko "desliga" a aderência e ergue o pé em 15 milissegundos. Ao contrário de uma fita adesiva, as cerdas ficam mais limpas com o uso, sem que o animal precise se limpar: poucos passos bastam, porque a sujeira adere mais à parede do que às poucas espátulas que a tocam. Cópias já existem: uma "fita de lagartixa" sustentou um boneco do Homem-Aranha de 40 gramas num teto de vidro, ainda que com aderência muito menor que a do animal.

fontes.titulo: Autumn et al. (2002). Evidence for van der Waals adhesion in gecko setae. PNAS
fontes.trecho: The mechanism of dry adhesion in the millions of setae on the toes of geckos has been the focus of scientific study for over a century. We provide the first direct experimental evidence for dry adhesion of gecko setae by van der Waals forces, and reject the use of mechanisms relying on high surface polarity, including capillary adhesion. The toes of live Tokay geckos were highly hydrophobic, and adhered equally well to strongly hydrophobic and strongly hydrophilic, polarizable surfaces. Adhesion of a single isolated gecko seta was equally effective on the hydrophobic and hydrophilic surfaces of a microelectro-mechanical systems force sensor. A van der Waals mechanism implies that the remarkable adhesive properties of gecko setae are merely a result of the size and shape of the tips, and are not strongly affected by surface chemistry.

Geckos are renowned for their exceptional ability to stick and run on any vertical and inverted surface (excluding Teflon). [...] the underside of a gecko toe typically bears a series of ridges, which are covered with uniform ranks of setae, and each seta further divides into hundreds of split ends and flat tips called spatulas [...] geckos manage to lift their feet so quickly – in just 15 milliseconds – with no measurable detachment forces. [...] by increasing the angle between the setal shaft and the substrate to 30 degrees, no matter how big the perpendicular adhesive force is, geckos 'turn off' the stickiness [...] Unlike conventional adhesives, gecko adhesive becomes cleaner with repeated use [...] geckos are not known to groom their feet in order to retain their adhesive properties – all they need is only a few steps to recover their ability to cling to vertical surfaces. [...] self-cleaning occurs by an energetic disequilibrium between the adhesive forces attracting a dirt particle to the substrate and those attracting the same particle to one or more spatulae. [...] The result of this "gecko tape" was tested by attaching a sample to the hand of a 15 cm high plastic Spider-Man figure weighing 40 g, which enabled it to stick to a glass ceiling [...] However, the adhesion coefficient was only 0.06, which is low compared with real geckos

Their surfaces can adhere to almost any type of material. [...] On its feet, the gecko has many microscopic hairs, or setae (singular seta), arranged into lamellae that increase the Van der Waals forces - the distance-dependent attraction between atoms or molecules - between its feet and the surface.

gancho: Um besouro da Namíbia de costas cheias de calombos ficou famoso por "beber neblina" e inspirou superfícies que coletam água. Só que o besouro do estudo famoso talvez nem colete neblina na natureza.
explicacao: No deserto do Namibe, onde chove pouquíssimo, a neblina da manhã é uma fonte de água. Em 2001, um artigo na revista Nature descreveu como um besouro tido como Stenocara capturaria essa água: calombos que atraem água, cercados por áreas cerosas que a repelem, juntariam gotículas até que elas ficassem pesadas e rolassem até a boca. Pesquisadores do MIT imitaram a ideia com superfícies que alternam materiais que atraem e repelem água, pensando em coletar umidade do ar e em vidros que não embaçam. Mas outros cientistas contestaram o ponto de partida. Eles argumentam que o besouro estudado nunca coleta neblina ativamente na natureza e o reidentificaram como outra espécie, Physasterna cribripes. Das cerca de 200 espécies de besouros da região, só duas foram vistas "tomando banho de neblina", de cabeça para baixo contra o vento, e ambas do gênero Onymacris, de costas lisas com sulcos, sem calombos. Num estudo de 2010 em câmara de neblina, das quatro espécies testadas, só Onymacris unguicularis assumiu a postura, e as diferenças na água colhida pelos vários tipos de carapaça foram pequenas. O mesmo estudo não encontrou áreas que atraem água nas carapaças de nenhuma das quatro espécies. A conclusão dos autores: o comportamento pesa mais que a textura das costas.

fontes.trecho: the racingstripe darkling beetle, is a species of beetle that is native to the Namib Desert in southern Africa. This is one of the most arid areas of the world [...] the droplets stick to hydrophilic bumps, which are surrounded by waxy, hydrophobic troughs. [...] at that point it will roll down the beetle's back to its mouthparts. Researchers at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology have emulated this capability by creating a textured surface that combines alternating hydrophobic and hydrophilic materials. Potential uses include extracting moisture from the air and creating fog-free windows and mirrors. [...] Parker, A. R. & C. R. Lawrence (2001). "Water capture by a desert beetle". Nature.

fontes.titulo: Nørgaard e Dacke (2010). Fog-basking behaviour and water collection efficiency in Namib Desert Darkling beetles. Frontiers in Zoology
fontes.trecho: Published: 16 July 2010 [...] In the Namib Desert fog represents an alternative water source. [...] Hamilton and co-authors do not challenge the mechanism presented for fog collection, but argue that the beetle studied to reveal this mechanism never actually actively collects fog water in nature. That fact that Hamilton and colleagues [9] also re-identify the model beetle in the study by Parker and Lawrence [10] as a Physasterna cribripes rather than a Stenocara sp. [...] A quick inspection of the two beetles that are well known to fog-bask - O. bicolor and O. unguicularis - reveals that the elytra of these beetle do not carry the numerous bumps [...] but rather have smooth elytra surfaces with regular grooves. [...] only two out of approximately 200 beetle species inhabiting this area have ever been observed to fog-bask - both from the genus Onymacris. [...] we found that the second largest O. unguicularis is the only one of the four beetles that assumes the head standing fog-basking behaviour [...] The differences in fog water harvesting efficiency by the dorsal surface areas of beetles with very different elytra surface structures were minor. We therefore conclude that the fog-basking behaviour itself is a more important factor than structural adaptations when O. unguicularis collect water from fog. [...] By adopting a head standing posture facing into the wind, the fog water collects on their elytra and runs down to their mouth [...] However, no hydrophilic areas could be identified either on the elytra, pronotum or head in any of our

gancho: O olho das mariposas quase não reflete luz, o que evita denunciá-las a predadores no escuro. O truque, saliências menores que o comprimento de onda da luz, foi copiado em lentes de câmera.
explicacao: A superfície do olho de uma mariposa é coberta por uma película natural nanoestruturada: um padrão hexagonal de saliências com cerca de 200 nanômetros de altura, com centros separados por 300 nanômetros. Como essas saliências são menores que o comprimento de onda da luz visível, a luz não as "vê" uma a uma. O que ela encontra é uma mudança gradual e contínua do índice de refração entre o ar e o olho, sem a fronteira brusca que causa o reflexo. Assim a mariposa enxerga bem no escuro sem que o brilho dos olhos revele onde ela está. Os antirreflexos comuns funcionam de outro jeito: camadas finas e transparentes, com espessuras escolhidas para que as reflexões nas várias interfaces se cancelem. A versão inspirada na mariposa já virou produto: a Canon usa a técnica no seu revestimento SWC, que reduz bastante os reflexos indesejados nas lentes. Estruturas desse tipo também são estudadas para diminuir a refletividade de painéis solares e aparecem em eletrodos experimentais para quebrar a água e produzir hidrogênio.

fontes.trecho: Moths' eyes have an unusual property: their surfaces are covered with a natural nanostructured film, which eliminates reflections. This allows the moth to see well in the dark, without reflections to give its location away to predators. The structure consists of a hexagonal pattern of bumps, each roughly 200 nm high and spaced on 300 nm centers. This kind of antireflective coating works because the bumps are smaller than the wavelength of visible light, so the light sees the surface as having a continuous refractive index gradient between the air and the medium, which decreases reflection by effectively removing the air-lens interface. Practical anti-reflective films have been made by humans using this effect; this is a form of biomimicry. Canon uses the moth-eye technique in their SWC subwavelength structure coating, which significantly reduces lens flare. Such structures are also used in photonic devices, for example, moth-eye structures grown from tungsten oxide and iron oxide can be used as photoelectrodes for splitting water to produce hydrogen [...] Many coatings consist of transparent thin film structures with alternating layers of contrasting refractive index. Layer thicknesses are chosen to produce destructive interference in the beams reflected from the interfaces
The light refractive properties of the moth's eye has been studied to reduce the reflectivity of solar panels.

gancho: As tachas refletivas "olho de gato" originais, criadas na Inglaterra em 1934, se limpam sozinhas: quando um carro passa, a borracha afunda e um limpador esfrega os refletores. Já o gato da história é incerto.
explicacao: O inglês Percy Shaw, de Halifax, patenteou em 1934 a tacha refletiva de estrada, apoiada numa patente de lente retrorrefletora de 1927, de Richard Hollins Murray. Há várias versões de como teve a ideia. A mais famosa: dirigindo à noite por uma estrada perigosa, com um barranco de um lado, ele teria visto um gato numa cerca refletir os faróis, o que o ajudou a corrigir a direção. Numa entrevista, porém, Shaw contou outra história, sobre levar para o chão os refletores das placas numa noite de neblina. E crianças que visitavam a fábrica nos anos 1970 ouviam que a inspiração foram trilhos de bonde polidos, que refletiam os faróis. O desenho original tinha dois pares de refletores numa cúpula de borracha branca, dentro de uma caixa de ferro fundido. A cúpula é flexível e afunda com a passagem dos carros; nesse momento, um limpador fixo de borracha esfrega os refletores, e a água de chuva acumulada na base melhora a limpeza. Nem toda tacha faz isso: as fixas, como a equivalente mais próxima usada nos EUA, não têm o mecanismo de autolimpeza. As vendas começaram devagar, mas a aprovação do governo e o blecaute da Segunda Guerra fizeram a produção passar de um milhão de unidades por ano.

fontes.trecho: He patented the reflective road stud or "cat's eye" in 1934 [...] Percy Shaw was born in Halifax [...] There are several stories about how he came up with the idea. The most famous involves his driving down the difficult road (Queensbury Road, part of the A647 with a very steep drop to one side) [...] when a cat on a fence along the edge of the road looked at the car and reflected his headlights back to him, allowing him to take corrective action and remain on the road. In an interview with Alan Whicker, however, he told a different story of being inspired on a foggy night to think of a way of moving the reflective studs on a road sign to the road surface. Further, local schoolchildren who were taken on visits to the factory in the late 1970s were told that the idea came from Shaw seeing light reflected from his car headlamps by tram tracks in the road on a foggy night. The tram tracks were polished by the passing of trams [...] In 1934, he patented his invention (patents Nos. 436,290 and 457,536), based on the 1927 retroreflecting lens patent of Richard Hollins Murray. [...] Sales were initially slow, but approval from the Ministry of Transport and the blackout in the Second World War gave a huge boost to production and the firm [...] grew in size making more than a million roadstuds a year

The original form consisted of two pairs of retroreflectors set into a white rubber dome, mounted in a cast iron housing. [...] A key feature of the cat's eye is the flexible rubber dome which is occasionally deformed by the passage of traffic. A fixed rubber wiper cleans the surface of the reflectors as they sink below the surface of the road (the base tends to hold water after a shower of rain, making this process even more efficient). [...] The closest equivalent in the United States is the Stimsonite retroreflective raised pavement marker, a fixed marker without the rubber self-cleaning property.

gancho: A vitória-régia da Amazônia ajudou a criar um ícone da Revolução Industrial. As nervuras da folha gigante inspiraram a estufa de Joseph Paxton, que levou ao Palácio de Cristal da Exposição de Londres de 1851.
explicacao: Na Inglaterra vitoriana, fazer florescer a enorme planta amazônica virou disputa entre aristocratas jardineiros. Sementes enviadas de lá ao jardim de Kew em 1836 germinaram, mas as plantas não floresciam. Em 1849, uma muda foi entregue a Joseph Paxton, jardineiro do duque de Devonshire em Chatsworth. Em dois meses, as folhas tinham 1,4 metro de diâmetro, e um mês depois veio a flor, a primeira na Inglaterra, que causou sensação. A filha de Paxton chegou a ser desenhada para os jornais em pé sobre uma das folhas. Como a planta crescia sem parar, foi preciso uma estufa maior, e Paxton achou a estrutura dela na própria folha, "uma façanha natural de engenharia": nervuras rígidas que irradiam do centro, ligadas por nervuras transversais flexíveis. Anos de experiências levaram ao modelo de estufa que inspirou o Palácio de Cristal, de ferro fundido e vidro, erguido no Hyde Park para a Grande Exposição de 1851. Paxton fez o primeiro esboço num mata-borrão cor-de-rosa durante uma reunião, e o prédio, de 564 metros de comprimento, ficou pronto em menos de um ano.

fontes.trecho: The next great building at Chatsworth was built for the first seeds of the Victoria regia lily which had been sent to Kew from the Amazon in 1836. Although they had germinated and grown they had not flowered and in 1849 a seedling was given to Paxton to try out at Chatsworth. [...] within two months the leaves were 4.5 ft (1.4 m) in diameter, and a month later it flowered. It continued growing and it became necessary to build a much larger house, the Victoria Regia House. Inspired by the waterlily's huge leaves – 'a natural feat of engineering' – he found the structure for his conservatory [...] The secret was in the rigidity provided by the radiating ribs connecting with flexible cross-ribs. Constant experimentation over a number of years led him to devise the glasshouse design that inspired the Crystal Palace.

The Crystal Palace was a cast iron and plate glass structure, originally built in Hyde Park, London, to house the Great Exhibition of 1851. [...] Designed by Joseph Paxton, the Great Exhibition building was 1,851 feet (564 m) long [...] Paxton made his original concept drawing, which he doodled onto a sheet of pink blotting paper. [...] Paxton was able to design and build the largest glass structure yet created, from scratch, in less than a year [...] in 1849 he caused a sensation in the horticultural world when he succeeded in producing the first amazonica flowers to be grown in England. His daughter Alice was drawn for the newspapers, standing on one of the leaves.
It was once the subject of rivalry between Victorian gardeners in England. [...] Joseph Paxton (for the Duke of Devonshire) being the first in November 1849

gancho: A borda da frente das nadadeiras da jubarte é cheia de calombos. Em vez de atrapalhar, eles evitam a perda brusca de sustentação nas curvas fechadas, e a ideia passou a ser testada em asas e turbinas.
explicacao: A jubarte é enorme, com 14 a 17 metros e até 40 toneladas, mas consegue fazer giros e voltas embaixo d'água. Ela é a única grande baleia com tubérculos, calombos na cabeça e na borda dianteira das nadadeiras. Nas nadadeiras, eles funcionam como pequenos geradores de vórtices. Sobre cada crista, o redemoinho empurra o fluxo para baixo e atrasa o estol, o descolamento do fluxo que faz uma asa perder sustentação de repente. Assim a nadadeira trabalha em ângulos mais inclinados e, quando o estol vem, a perda é gradual, não súbita. Isso ajuda nas curvas fechadas que a baleia faz quando caça com redes de bolhas. Num dos primeiros estudos, com modelagem em computador, os pesquisadores Watts e Fish estimaram 4,8% a mais de sustentação num perfil com tubérculos. Outros trabalhos mostraram um custo: os tubérculos podem baixar a sustentação máxima, em troca de uma perda mais suave depois do estol. Esses resultados levaram a aplicar a ideia em asas de avião e em turbinas industriais e eólicas, e há estudos indicando até 20% a mais de geração em turbinas. Mas a água impõe um porém: nos vales entre os calombos pode haver cavitação, com bolhas que reduzem a sustentação e fazem barulho. E a própria literatura diz que falta pesquisa para levar o efeito a aviões e à geração de energia.

fontes.trecho: Despite their large size, these whales are agile and are able to perform rolls and loops underwater. Research on humpback whales indicated that the presence of these tubercles on the leading edge of whale fins reduced stall and increased lift, while reducing noise in the post-stall regime. Researchers were motivated by these positive results to apply these concepts to aircraft wings as well as industrial and wind turbines. Early research on this topic was performed by Watts & Fish followed by further experiments both in water and wind tunnels. Watts & Fish determined that the presence of tubercles on the leading edge of airfoil increased lift by 4.8%. [...] In the post-stall regime, foils with tubercles experienced a gradual loss of lift as opposed to foils without tubercles, which experienced a sudden loss of lift. [...] These vortical structures impose a downward deflection of the airflow (downwash) over the crests of tubercles. This downward deflection delays stall on the airfoil. [...] However, in water, due to the crest/trough structure, cavitation is possible, and is undesirable. [...] These bubbles reduce lift and increase drag, while increasing noise in the flow when the bubbles collapse. [...] more research is needed in order to apply the knowledge of the tubercle effect to industrial, aircraft, or energy applications. [...] It was also observed in turbine design that leading-edge effects have the ability to improve power generation by a factor of up to 20%. [...] Using computational modeling, it was determined that the presence of tubercles produces a delay in the angle of attack until stall [...] Leading-edge tubercles have been found to reduce the point of maximum lift and increase the region of post-stall lift.

Adults range in length from 14–17 m (46–56 ft) and weigh up to 40 metric tons [...] Unique among large whales, humpbacks have bumps or tubercles on the head and front edge of the flippers [...] The tubercles on the flippers stall the angle of attack, which both maximizes lift and minimizes drag (see tubercle effect). This, along with the shape of the flippers, allows the whales to make the abrupt turns necessary during bubble-feeding.

gancho: O azul intenso das asas da borboleta-morfo não vem de pigmento, e sim de estruturas microscópicas que fazem a luz interferir consigo mesma. Copiando isso, criaram fibras coloridas sem nenhum corante.
explicacao: Na coloração estrutural, a cor nasce de superfícies com estruturas tão finas que interferem com a luz visível, em vez de pigmentos. Nas escamas das asas de algumas borboletas Morpho, dos trópicos, essas estruturas são arranjos de quitina em forma de árvore, e o resultado é um azul vibrante. O fenômeno é conhecido há séculos: os ingleses Robert Hooke e Isaac Newton foram os primeiros a descrever esse tipo de cor, e Thomas Young explicou o princípio, a interferência de ondas, um século depois. A indústria copiou a ideia. A japonesa Teijin criou o Morphotex, tecido sem tingimento feito de fibras com 61 camadas planas alternadas de náilon e poliéster, cada uma com 70 a 100 nanômetros de espessura, dentro de uma capa transparente. Como os dois plásticos desviam a luz de forma diferente, as camadas geram cor por interferência; foram produzidas fibras vermelhas, verdes, azuis e violeta. Em 2010, a estilista Donna Sgro fez um vestido com ele. Antes, em 2007, a Qualcomm lançou as telas Mirasol, que formavam a imagem com interferência óptica do mesmo tipo da que colore a Morpho.

fontes.trecho: Structural coloration in animals, and a few plants, is the production of colour by microscopically structured surfaces fine enough to interfere with visible light instead of pigments [...] Structural coloration was first described by English scientists Robert Hooke and Isaac Newton, and its principle—wave interference—explained by Thomas Young a century later. [...] Another way to produce a diffraction grating is with tree-shaped arrays of chitin, as in the wing scales of some of the brilliantly coloured tropical Morpho butterflies [...] In 2010, the dressmaker Donna Sgro made a dress from Teijin Fibers' Morphotex, an undyed fabric woven from structurally coloured fibres, mimicking the microstructure of Morpho butterfly wing scales. The fibres are composed of 61 flat alternating layers, between 70 and 100 nanometres thick, of two plastics with different refractive indices, nylon and polyester, in a transparent nylon sheath with an oval cross-section. [...] The fibres have been produced in red, green, blue, and violet.

Morpho butterfly wings are structurally coloured to produce a vibrant blue that does not vary with angle. [...] In 2007, Qualcomm commercialised an interferometric modulator display technology, "Mirasol", using Morpho-like optical interference.
